lawyer:
Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur with, Mr. Abbas Uddin, Advocates, For the petitioner.
Mr. Fakir Abdul Mannan, Advocate, For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Abdul Wahed Mia ------ Petitioner
Vs
Saira Khatun ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
"The opposite party No. 1 Saira Khatoon as plaintiff filed the aforesaid suit in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for eviction of the defendant petitioner from the suit premises on the allegations interalia that the defendant was a defaulter in respect of payment of the house rent for the month of March, 1983; that the defendant was is also a defaulter for his irregular deposit of rent in the House Rent Control Case No. 247 of 1963; that the plaintiff bonafide requires the suit premises premises for her son's garrage; that the plaintiff served notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act upon the defendant on 8.5.85 but inspite of that the defendant failed to vacate the suit premises. Hence the aforesaid suit for eviction." 

 3. The petitioner as defendant contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint and contending inter-alia that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and the same was barred by the principles of estoppel, acquiescence and waiver; that no notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was in fact upon the defendant and he did not receive any such notice from the side of the plaintiff; that the defendant was is not at all a defaulter and the suit premises is not at all required by the plaintiff for the purpose of Barrage. It has been further stated in the written statement that the suit premises is a shop in which the defendant as a tenant has been running his business since September, 1971 initially at a monthly rent of Tk. 100/ - and then from March, 1975 the monthly rent was enhanced to Tk. 200/- and thereafter on 11.2.82 as desired by the plaintiff the defendant petitioner paid in advance the entire rent for 12 months i. e. from January to December, 1982 at a further enhanced monthly rent at the rate of Tk. 275/-; thereafter the plaintiff received a rental of Tk. 275/00 for the month of January, 1983 in due course on granting and signing rent receipt. Thereafter the defendant offered Tk. 275/- as rent for the month of February, 1983 but the plaintiffs son refused to accept the same on the plea that his mother instructed him not to accept the same unless the defendant was ready to pay rent at the rate of Tk.1,000/- per month. In these circumstances the defendant sent a sum of Tk. 275/- as rent for the month of February, 1983 to the plaintiff by postal money, order dated 8.3.83 and the same was accepted and received by the plaintiff. The defendant thereafter on 10.4.83 sent the rent for the month of March, 1983 to the plaintiff by postal money order but the same was returned with the remarks that payment could not be effected since the payee had gone to Calcutta. Thereafter the defendant on the advice of his lawyer bonafide sent rents for the months of March and April. 1983 together to the plaintiff by Money order dated 8.5.83 which again was returned to the defendant on 25.5.83 with the same type of remarks. Thereafter the plaintiff started the House Rent Case No. 247 of 1983 on 4.6.83 and deposited the rent for the months of March and April, 1983 on 6.6.83 through Chalan. The defendant failed to succeed in the House Rent Control Case before the House Rent Controller which was contested by the plaintiff. The defendant then preferred appeal which was dismissed on 31.8.87 and against the said decision a Civil Revision Case being No. 254 of 1987 was pending in this High Court Division. It has been stated further that the defendant-petitioner has been still regularly depositing the rents in the Office of the House Rent Controller and thus the defendant-petitioner was/is not a defaulter at all. 

 4. On behalf of the plaintiff, her son alone as P.W. 1 was examined in this case and the defendant-petitioner examined 2 witnesses including himself in support of his case and filed a number of documents namely Exts. A-A (4) showing dispatch of rents by money orders. Exts. B-B (13) the rent receipts and Exts C-C (71) showing deposit of rent in House Rent Control Case No. 247 of 1983 by Chalans. On behalf of the plaintiff some documents were also filed namely Exts. 1 and 1(Ka) i.e. the copy of Judgments passed in House Rent Control Case as well as the Misc. Appeal No. 24 of 1985 and also Ext. 2 as copy of the legal notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. But neither any registration receipt nor any acknowledgment receipt in original was filed; only a photo- of the acknowledgement receipt namely Ext. 2(A) was filed in court allegedly bearing the signature of the defendant without its original or any explanation for such non-production of the same. It has been further stated in the written statement that the suit premises including the entire building absolutely belongs to the plaintiff but P.W. 1 her son has not got no share in it and the suit premises comprises 8 kathas of land, upon which the 2 storied building with 10/11 rooms in the ground floor including 5 shops and some open vacant space is situated. Hence there is no bonafide requirement of the plaintiff on the above averments the defendant contested the suit and prayed for its dismissed with costs. The learned Judge framed the following issues for consideration: 

 The learned S.C.C. Judge then on consideration of the materials on record and the facts and circumstances of the case decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree dated 11.10.89 particularly on the findings, inter alia that the defendant was is a defaulter and the plaintiff  bonafide required the suit premises and further that the defendant received the notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the defendant petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr Fakir Abdul Mannan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party on the other hand has submitted that the defendant-petitioner was and is a defaulter and the plaintiff-opposite party bonafide requires the suit premises for the use of her son as a garrage. In respect of the service of the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act upon the defendant-petitioner, the learned Advocate frankly concedes to the submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner to the effect that other finding of the trial court as regards service of notice has been based on inadmissible evidence. Thereafter without making further submission he souhgt for adjournment of the hearing of the case in order to enable him to take some steps in the matter and accordingly on his prayer, further hearing of the case was adjourned then again when the case appeared in the cause list as part heard on 5.3.92 he took further time and then filed an application on 8.3.92 under Order 23 rule 1 of Code of Civil Procedure with a copy to the other side for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to file a suit afresh on the same subject matter contending interalia in paragraph 2 of the application as follows:- 

 "That the hearing of the above case has started and at this stage it is found that there is want or proper service of the notice under Section 106 of the T.P. Act and on account of such formal defect the claim of this plaintiff-opposite party will fail. Hence, it is considered necessary that the main suit being S.C.C. Suit No. 166 of 1992 of the Assistant Judge, 1st Court Dhaka be with drawn with liberty to bring afresh suit on the same cause of action If not barred by any law, otherwise this plaintiff-opposite party will be highly prejudiced and will suffer loss and injuries;" 

 7. Thereafter, the matter was heard in presence of both the sides and today it is for judgment. It may be pointed out that the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner has raised no objection to the prayer of the plaintiff-opposite party for withdrawal of the suit at this stage with liberty to sue afresh. It is contended by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff that service of the legal notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is mandatory in a suit for eviction of a tenant and in the instant case he frankly admits that there has not been due service of the said notice by the plaintiff and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed, though the notice has nothing to do with the merit of the suit, The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party candidly submits that want of due service of the legal notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is a formal defect in the suit and there is no denying of the fact that there is want of due and proper service of such notice upon the defendant petitioner in the present suit, through the trial court wrongly found otherwise. He also submits that this formal defect ought to have been pointed out earlier in the trial court or in this court at the beginning of the hearing of the case, but because of his own bonafide mistake and over sightedness due to old age he could not do so and for this his client however should not suffer when law provides that withdrawal simplicity of a suit may be effected under Order 23 rule 1(1) C.P.C. even without any permission or leave of the court at any stage; but for withdrawal of a suit with liberty to sue afresh on the selfsame matter, permission or leave of the Court is necessary according to sub-rule(2) of rule 1 Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in the instant case though the application for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to sue afresh on the selfsame matter has been made at this stage in revision, yet there is no legal bar in granting such application in as much as this revision is a subsequent proceeding which follows from the results of the original suit and may have the effect of reopening the decree passed in the suit and as such the provision of Order 23 rule 1 are quite applicable in this case. His further submission is that the leave under Order 23 rule 1 is discretionary with the court but that discretion has to be exercised properly and judicially in the facts and circumstances of each case. As to the formal defect in a suit he further contends that it is well settled in a number of decisions of our court and some other Courts of the Subcontinent that formal defect or mistake should be given a wide and liberal meaning in the interest of justice which will have no bearing on the merit of the case. He also contends in this connection that there is nothing to be prejudiced by the other side, if the application is allowed after setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner does not oppose the application and the prayer of the plaintiff for withdrawal of the suit with leave to sue afresh if the cause of action is not time barred, but he humbly prays that as the application for withdrawal has been filed at this belated stage, his client, the defendant should be awarded some costs to be paid by the plaintiff. 

 8. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides perused the application and other materials on record and I find much substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff in respect of his application for withdrawal of the suit with permission to sue afresh on the same cause of action. I have also examined the relevant provisions of law and some decisions cited at the bar in this connection namely decisions reported in 25 D.L.R 485, and A.I.R. 1934 All. 450 and I am in full agreement with views expressed in the above decisions to the effect that the formal defect of "other Sufficient grounds" as under sub rule 2 of rule I of Order 23 C.P.C., should be liberally construed and there is no legal bar in granting an application for withdrawal of a suit with liberty a file a suit afresh on the selfsame matter even at the revisional stage provided the other requirements of the aforesaid provisions of law are fully complied with. In the instant case as I have already stated that there is no objection to the application and the prayer of the plaintiff under Order 23 rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure by the defendant petitioner, I need not go further into this matter for any other consideration. In the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice, the application which appears to be a bonafide one should be allowed without making any further observation or finding as to the submission of the learned Advocates on the other points involved in this case.
